$comment: Source of truth for the download site. tools/generate-download-site.py reads this file
and the code, and writes site/index.html. Nothing about a download is hardcoded in the
generator, so a page can never claim a file the pipeline does not produce.
`published` is false until a release exists. The page renders an honest 'not yet
published' state with the reason rather than a link that 404s, because a download page
whose buttons all fail is worse than one that says the build is not out yet.
`asset` is the stable filename the release workflow copies each bundle to. Tauri picks its
own names for MSIs and NSIS installers, which embed the upstream Tauri template version;
copying to a stable name means a URL published today still resolves after an upgrade.

product.name: Sentinel
product.tagline: Local-first network visibility and threat detection.
product.summary: Sentinel watches the traffic on your machine, reconstructs the connections that carry it, stores what it finds in a local database, and tells you what is happening. No account, no cloud service, nothing leaves the machine.

repositories.label: IklwaLabs
repositories.note: Primary repository. Ask IklwaLabs for access.

release.unpublished_reason: No GitHub release exists yet for v0.1.0. Tagging the repository starts the build matrix; the artifacts appear here once the release job has published them.

platforms.name: Windows
platforms.privilege: Run as Administrator. Reading frames needs an elevated token; Sentinel reports this through 'sentinel doctor' rather than failing at capture time.
platforms.summary: NSIS installer and MSI for x86-64. Captures from any adapter Npcap exposes, including a dedicated loopback adapter when Npcap is installed in full mode.
install: Install Npcap from npcap.com first. It is the capture driver; the installer does not bundle it.
Run Sentinel-0.1.0-windows-x64-setup.exe. The MSI is there if you prefer Windows Installer.
Launch Sentinel from the Start menu and choose an interface in the sidebar.

artifacts.label: NSIS installer
artifacts.detail: Recommended. Installs and adds a Start menu entry.

platforms.name: Linux
platforms.privilege: Grant the binary CAP_NET_RAW rather than running everything as root: sudo setcap cap_net_raw,cap_net_admin=eip /path/to/sentinel
platforms.summary: Debian package and AppImage for x86-64. Loopback capture is supported directly, so local traffic between processes on the machine is visible.
install: or make the AppImage executable and run it: chmod +x Sentinel-0.1.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage
sudo setcap cap_net_raw,cap_net_admin=eip /usr/bin/sentinel   # instead of running as root
Run 'sentinel doctor' to confirm capture is possible in your session.

artifacts.label: AppImage
artifacts.detail: No install step. chmod +x, then run.

platforms.name: macOS
platforms.privilege: The process must belong to the access_bpcap group, or run with sudo. An administrator has to arrange this.
platforms.summary: Disk image and application bundle, universal (Apple silicon and Intel). Unsigned: Gatekeeper refuses to open it until the quarantine attribute is cleared.
install: Open Sentinel-0.1.0-macos-universal.dmg and drag Sentinel to Applications.
The bundle is not notarised. Right-click it and choose Open, or clear the quarantine flag:
Capture additionally needs access_bpcap membership, which an administrator grants.

artifacts.label: Application bundle
artifacts.detail: For moving it between machines without a disk image.

platforms.name: Android
platforms.privilege: None. Android grants no capture privileges to an ordinary app.
platforms.summary: Analysis only. The APK lists interfaces and analyses PCAP files offline. Live capture is not implemented and the build reports it as unavailable instead of failing at runtime.
install: Enable developer mode and USB debugging on the device.
Sideload Sentinel-0.1.0-android.apk with adb install, or from the device's file manager.
Open a PCAP file from local storage to analyse it. Live capture is not available.

artifacts.label: APK
artifacts.detail: Sideload. Offline PCAP analysis only; no live capture.

features.title: Enumerates real capture interfaces
features.body: Through Npcap on Windows, libpcap on Linux and macOS. Wired, wireless, loopback, tunnel and virtual adapters are classified, and an adapter that cannot be captured says why instead of being offered.

features.title: Captures live traffic
features.body: From a selected adapter, on a dedicated thread, with backpressure that is counted rather than hidden. An ingress queue that overflows is visible in the interface.

features.title: Decodes L2 to L4 itself
features.body: Ethernet, VLAN, IPv4, IPv6, ARP, TCP, UDP and ICMP through an own bounds-checked decoder, so truncation and IP fragmentation are handled explicitly rather than guessed at.

features.title: Reconstructs bidirectional flows
features.body: Keyed on a canonically ordered endpoint pair with initiator detection from port roles, so a connection appears once with both directions attributed correctly.

features.title: Analyses PCAP files through the same pipeline
features.body: Offline results match live capture exactly, because there is one decoder and one flow engine behind both.

features.title: Reports incomplete data as incomplete
features.body: Packet loss is tracked separately for the driver, the ingress queue and the decoder, and every surface says which of the three lost frames.

features.title: Stores everything in SQLite, locally
features.body: One batched writer thread, append-only migrations, configurable retention. There is no code path that opens an outbound connection.

not_implemented.title: Threat rules
not_implemented.body: No detection engine ships in this release. The rule model and its evaluation contract are designed in docs/DETECTION_ENGINE.md, but presenting a rule that cannot fire would be worse than showing nothing.

not_implemented.title: Process attribution
not_implemented.body: Sentinel reports which process owns a connection only where the platform exposes it without a kernel driver. Nothing is guessed from port numbers.

not_implemented.title: Device inventory
not_implemented.body: There is no list of devices on the network. Sentinel observes this machine's traffic, not the topology around it.

not_implemented.title: DNS correlation
not_implemented.body: DNS queries are decoded and shown as flows. They are not resolved into hostnames or joined against other traffic yet.

build_from_source.prerequisites: Rust 1.95 or newer, Node.js 20 or newer, and a capture driver: Npcap with its SDK on Windows, libpcap-dev on Linux, nothing on macOS.
commands: cd apps/desktop/frontend && npm install && npm run build
notes: The custom-protocol feature is not optional. Without it the desktop binary looks for the Vite dev server instead of the assets embedded in the executable, and opens a black window.
The repository is private. You need an invitation from IklwaLabs to clone it.
docs/Sentinel-Reference.pdf is the whole product in one document: architecture, how to run it, how to control it, troubleshooting.

verification.body: Every platform's artifact set includes a SHA256SUMS.txt. Compare it before running anything:
notes: Artifacts are served over TLS from the GitHub release, so the checksum is a check against tampering in transit, not against a compromised account.
macOS artifacts are unsigned. That is why the checksum matters more there than elsewhere.

faq.a: No. There is no code path in Sentinel that opens an outbound connection. The database is a local SQLite file, and the interface is local. SECURITY.md documents this and the reasoning behind it.

faq.q: Why does capture fail on Windows until I run as Administrator?
faq.a: Reading frames needs an elevated token. Sentinel reports 'notElevated' through 'sentinel doctor' before you start a session, rather than failing later with a driver error code.

faq.q: Why is the macOS build unsigned?
faq.a: Notarisation needs an Apple developer account. Until there is one, right-click the app and choose Open, or clear the quarantine attribute. The SHA256SUMS.txt file lets you verify the download first.

faq.q: Can the Android build capture live traffic?
faq.a: No. It needs a userspace TCP/IP stack over an app-owned VPN slot, which is not implemented. The APK analyses PCAP files and lists interfaces, and reports live capture as unavailable rather than pretending.
In a SQLite database under your platform's application-data directory, named by sentinel-platform so each platform uses its own conventions. 'sentinel version' reports the schema version.
Not in this release. The product is named for it and the roadmap commits to it, but v0.1.0 ships the capture-to-storage pipeline and none of the rules. docs/DETECTION_ENGINE.md explains the design.
